hook: AP draws *15,000 cusecs* from Sagar; Telangana matches it
hook_b: AP draws *15,000 cusecs* from Sagar; Telangana matches it
tldr: Tension at Nagarjunasagar on Thursday after Andhra Pradesh released water through the right canal without prior information, Telangana Today reported.

beats.what: About 15,000 cusecs flowed to AP via the right canal; Telangana officials then released 15,000 cusecs from the left canal.
beats.why: Telangana officials charged AP with drawing water without informing them.
beats.care: Both states share Krishna water stored at Sagar, which is tight in a dry year.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: This adds to the row over AP's Palnadu Water Grid project, which Telangana says lacks permission. Irrigation Minister Uttam Kumar Reddy had not responded yet, the report said.

cards.q: Who should settle Sagar water releases?

qs: Without telemetry, how do the states agree on how much each has drawn?

facts.t: Only *18* telemetry stations measure Krishna water use, so drawals are hard to verify.

viz.verdict: Equal releases on both sides as the two states dispute the drawal.

learn.t: Cusec = one cubic foot of water flowing per second

watch: Whether the Krishna River Management Board steps in.

sources.name: Telangana Today
sources.title: Telangana, Andhra Pradesh spar over water release at Nagarjunasagar

fact: AP released *15,000 cusecs* from Nagarjunasagar without notice; Telangana released the same
twist: AP said the water was for *drinking needs*; Telangana officials called it unauthorised.
